scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8871: host_2_1_1_1 (10.2.1.2) reports it has lost everything
beyond its own gateway: every 10.200.0.x server times out, and it cannot reach
host_1_1_1_1 in the other pod either. It CAN still ping its gateway 10.2.1.1.
Pod 1 is unaffected -- host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm normally. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on router_core_2 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_2 ospfd
Mechanism: router_core_2 is pod 2's only way out: switch_dist_2_1's single
  uplink (172.16.0.8/31, area 1) terminates on router_core_2, which as the
  pod-2 ABR carries 10.2.1.0/24 between area 1 and the area-0 backbone. With
  ospfd killed, zebra flushes router_core_2's OSPF routes immediately, so
  pod-2 traffic arriving at router_core_2 has no route and dies there; the
  other routers then age out router_core_2's LSAs and withdraw 10.2.1.0/24.
  Pod 1 (host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> router_core_3 -> farm)
  never transits router_core_2, so it stays healthy.
Localization: router_core_2
Root cause: ospfd not running on router_core_2
Fix: restart FRR on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on router_core_2" -- that is the same fault observed at the
config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).
Unlike the vtysh-provisioned Kath labs, this topology keeps its OSPF config
in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process, not the file), so a
plain restart reloads the full configuration, OSPF re-converges, and pod 2
regains connectivity.
scoring_axes: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: FRRouting/OSPF control-plane on router_core_2.
- Mechanism: Host 10.2.1.2 (host_2_1_1_1) can reach its default gateway 10.2.1.1 (switch_dist_2_1), but any off-subnet traffic fails because the gateway has no routes beyond its directly connected networks. Pings from host_2_1_1_1 to 10.200.0.2 return “From 10.2.1.1 Destination Net Unreachable,” which is an ICMP generated by the gateway when it lacks a route.
- Localization: On switch_dist_2_1, OSPF is configured but has no neighbors (show ip ospf neighbor is empty). Its Linux routing table contains only connected routes 10.2.1.0/24 (br0) and 172.16.0.8/31 (uplink) and no learned routes. The uplink peer router_core_2 shows no FRR/OSPF configuration (vtysh running-config has no router ospf stanza) and “ospfd is not running.” Conversely, router_core_1 and router_core_3 have OSPF routes present, matching the report that Pod 1 is unaffected.
- Root cause: FRR/OSPF is stopped or missing configuration on router_core_2, preventing an OSPF adjacency on 172.16.0.8/31 to switch_dist_2_1 and isolating Pod 2 from the rest of the network.
- Corrective fix: Restore and start FRR/OSPF on router_core_2 with the correct OSPF configuration for all its core links (including 172.16.0.8/31 toward switch_dist_2_1) and appropriate areas. After starting, verify “show ip ospf neighbor” on both router_core_2 and switch_dist_2_1 shows adjacency and that switch_dist_2_1 learns routes to 10.200.0.0/24 and 10.1.1.0/24. This will restore reachability for host_2_1_1_1 to servers and Pod 1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to router_core_2, stating ospfd/FRR is stopped/missing on that device.
The report explicitly states ospfd/FRR/OSPF is not running on router_core_2 (OSPF daemon down), satisfying the axis.

per_axis.axis: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes Pod 1 is unaffected and references servers/the farm remaining reachable, isolating the failure to Pod 2's transit via router_core_2.
Proposes restarting/starting FRR/OSPF on router_core_2 and restoring its OSPF config so adjacencies and routes are learned, which matches the expected fix.

The logs directly show ospfd is not running on router_core_2 (vtysh running-config empty, frr service inactive) and that switch_dist_2_1 has no OSPF neighbors and returns ICMP ‘Destination Net Unreachable’, so the conclusion that pod-2 is isolated because router_core_2’s OSPF/FRR is down follows logically and is well-supported.
